A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LEDOM and Reverse Reward work despite the shortened title. Text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations in Tables 2 and 4, training-loss curves in Figure 4, and generated outputs and mathematical reasoning case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations in Tables 5 and 3, the training-loss curves, and the case studies in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The reverse-token training objective, 2B/7B architectures, combined forward/reverse reward, response reranking, and step-wise beam search remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both use the same DCLM/MAP-Neo pretraining corpus, OpenMathInstruct-2 fine-tuning data, general NLP benchmarks, four mathematical benchmarks, and qualitative task scenarios. Moving the general benchmark table to the appendix does not alter coverage.

E2.justification: Both retain size-matched FLMs for general evaluation and the same DeepSeekMath, QwenMath, and OpenMath2 comparisons using Greedy Decoding and Best-of-N (Random). Comparator membership within the reported experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 2.3 changes the reported pretraining warmup from 0.55% of total steps to 2,000 iterations. This resolves a conflict with v1 Appendix A.2 and Table 6, which already specified 2,000; it does not establish that training was rerun. Evaluation procedures and inference budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The sampling-size analysis with N from 1 to 64, training-dynamics analysis, representative generation cases, and mathematical reranking/beam-search case studies are retained. Figures 3–4 and Appendix D.4 provide the same evidence.

E5.justification: Both report fine-tuning seed 0 in Appendix D.2.2 and retain the same statistical reporting practices. No repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates are added.

E6.justification: All general benchmark entries match between v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 5, and mathematical results match between v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 3. For example, QwenMath with Reverse Reward remains at 80.8 on MATH-500 and 96.1 on GSM8K. Plotted results and qualitative outputs are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The autoregressive factorizations, training loss, prompt definitions, and Reverse Reward equations retain the same mathematical content. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: Despite shortening the title, the abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of a purely reverse-trained foundational model, distinctive generation behavior, and improved mathematical reasoning through Reverse Reward.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning reverse-prediction uncertainty, forward-task weaknesses, complementary reward signals, and safety remain intact. The limitations concerning scale, English-focused evaluation, and training recipes are unchanged; the revised case-study introduction mainly accommodates section reordering.

D1.justification: The warmup documentation is corrected to consistently specify 2,000 iterations. Other optimizer, precision, and hardware details expanded in Section 2.3 were already documented in v1 Appendix A.2 and Table 6. Fine-tuning details and model/code/data release statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 7 and the cited-work inventory retain the same comparisons with bidirectional, reverse-training, reversal-curse, and infilling research. The substantive novelty positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'LEDOM: An Open and Fundamental Reverse Language Model' to 'Reverse Language Model'. Evaluation and Case-Based Exploration exchange order, their transitions and references are adjusted, and Section 2.3 summarizes existing appendix details. Most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The general benchmark table moves from main-text Table 2 to appendix Table 5, while the case-study table moves earlier and becomes Table 2. Appendix figures and pseudocode also shift position. These are localized relocations and layout adjustments; figure content and table structures remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves the contradictory warmup descriptions by aligning Section 2.3 with the appendix's 2,000 iterations and fixes the erroneous appendix reference, modestly improving the reliability of the training specification. Moving the general benchmark table to the appendix makes it less immediate to consult, but all evidence remains available. The overall gain is limited.
